newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian stocks end at record highs, more gains seen.
newsitem.headline: Belgian stocks end at record highs, more gains seen.

text.p: U.S. data and other factors sent Belgian shares to new record highs on Tuesday and analysts expected the market to continue to benefit in the days ahead from stock-positive economic fundamentals.
The Bel-20 index ended at a new closing high of 2,234.98 points, up 0.80 percent on the day, after earlier setting a new all-time high of 2,241.72 points.

The main factor driving Belgian shares higher was data confirming the U.S. economy was under control and lessening fears of a new rise in U.S. interest rates. But Belgian bank merger speculation and coupon hunting also played a part.

With the dividend season about to start, Corluy & Co strategist Stefan Casteleyn said that deflationary government fiscal policies in Europe would continue to make stocks more attractive than bonds to investors looking for extra yield.

"You could even say that interest rates in Europe are too high compared with the level of economic growth and inflation we have at the moment," Casteleyn said. "If you can imagine interest rates going down more, it's certain we have not seen the end of the bull run in Europe."
Belgian inflation was 1.26 percent in April, down from 1.46 percent in March, the economics ministry said on Tuesday.
Banks led the Brussels bourse higher on Tuesday, thanks to continued speculation about the creation of a Big Belgian Bank and buying ahead of dividend payments next week.

Kredietbank was the main beneficiary, rising 3.87 percent to 14,100 francs after controlling shareholder Almanij said at the weekend its family shareholders might be willing to back an alliance with another institution.

Bank BBL, which holds its annual shareholders meeting on Wednesday at which chief executive officer Michel Tilmant is expected to be questioned on the Big Belgian Bank, ended up 210 francs at a new all-time high of 8,850 francs.
Dexia CC continued to rebound, adding 1.86 percent to 3,560 francs, following losses last week on news its controlling shareholder planned to sell more shares in the bank.

However, fast food retailer Quick ended unchanged at 1,780 francs on news that the Henderson fund group had cut its stake in the company to 3.16 percent from 6.74 percent. Dealers took Henderson's statement as an explanation for the stock's recent underperformance.
Non ferrous metals group Union Miniere also surprised dealers with a 3.25 percent fall to 2,830 francs. "Maybe its profit taking," one commented.
